newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds tread water, buyers seen returning.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds tread water, buyers seen returning.

text.p: Danish bond prices were mixed or slightly lower on Thursday in a quiet market with dealers foreseeing growing buyer interest.
"Activity has been better than yesterday, buyer interest is good with the lower prices," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was unchanged from the start at 112.22, yielding 6.14 percent in 1.8 billion crown turnover with the seven percent 2007 forthcoming benchmark 0.02 point lower at 104.86 with 6.34 percent yield and turnover at 1.4 billion crowns.
The 2006's September future rose 0.26 point to 111.38 with one contract traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.42 point to 90.45.
The crown traded at 3.8078 per mark at 1150 gmt, down a touch from around 3.8070 at the opening.

The 2006's 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 42 basis points with the 2007-bund differential at an unaltered 62. The Central Bank was active on the market selling some 250 million crowns worth of mid-term paper as part of its routine financing operations.
